patch_description: The annealed soft-min/soft-max L-BFGS approach plateaus near 0.24 because gradient steps treat all pairwise distances nearly uniformly, while the true objective depends only on the min-distance pair and max-distance pair. Add a fast, targeted hill-climb that (a) pushes the closest pair of points directly apart along their separating direction, and (b) pulls the farthest pair inward along theirs, with adaptive step sizes and a shrinking geometric schedule. These moves act exactly on the binding constraints of dmin/dmax, so they can squeeze out extra ratio that coordinate-based optimizers miss. Insert it as Phase 4 before normalization, and trim Phase 2/3 trial counts slightly to offset added runtime (current eval_time 51.88s is high; keep under timeout). The hill-climb is cheap (O(n^2) per iteration, no gradients), and since every accepted move must strictly increase the true ratio, it can only improve the returned configuration.
